drivingQuestion: What premise underlies each side of the half-damage dispute?

segments.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר פַּלְגָא נִיזְקָא מָמוֹנָא, קָסָבַר: סְתָם שְׁוָורִים לָאו בְּחֶזְקַת שִׁימּוּר קָיְימִי. וּבְדִין הוּא דִּמְשַׁלֵּם כּוּלֵּיהּ, וְרַחֲמָנָא הוּא דְּחָיֵיס עִלָּוֵיהּ, דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא אִיַּעַד תּוֹרָא. רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר פַּלְגָא נִיזְקָא קְנָסָא, קָסָבַר: סְתָם שְׁוָורִים בְּחֶזְקַת שִׁימּוּר קָיְימִי. וּבְדִין הוּא דְּלָא לִישַׁלֵּם כְּלָל, וְרַחֲמָנָא הוּא דְּקַנְסֵיהּ, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנִינְטְרֵיהּ לְתוֹרֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates. «Rav Pappa said: Half the damage» is considered a payment of «money,» as «he maintains: Standard oxen do not exist in the presumptive status of safety,» and therefore are likely to cause damage. «And by right,» the owner «should pay the entire» damage caused by his animal, «and it is the Merciful One that has compassion on him, as his ox is not yet forewarned» until it has gored a person or an animal three times. Fundamentally, the payment is for damage that the animal caused. «Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said» that «half the damage» is payment of a «fine,» as «he maintains: Standard oxen exist in the presumptive status of safety,» and are not dangerous. «And by right,» the owner «should not pay at all,» as the ox goring could not have been anticipated, and therefore the owner bears no responsibility. «And it is the Merciful One that penalized him so that he would guard his ox.» The sum that he pays is a fine.
